## The problem

Balancing a five-faction wargame by hand is slow, and play-testers are scarce. The question is whether AI-vs-AI round-robins with counterfactual stat changes can detect over- or under-powered units before release.

## Approach

A Python port of the game's combat, board and turn engine, with unit data checked against the live game's source. A masked actor-critic trained with PPO against periodically frozen copies of itself. A 5x5 faction round-robin evaluator, and a counterfactual tool that applies stat overrides in memory and compares matchup matrices. A predecessor prototype on a tabletop ruleset developed the self-play env and a premature-convergence (entropy) monitor.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Automated adjudication and COA stress-testing face the same threat: an optimising agent exploits the scoring rule, so outcome deltas stop measuring the effect of interest. The project shows the design of a counterfactual round-robin, the need for a measured noise floor before reading deltas, and how draw-rate confounding produced wrong-sign conclusions.
:::

|---|---|

| Engine self-consistency test suite (wound table, closed-form vs Monte Carlo ranged and melee damage, line of sight, pathfinding, deployment zones, action masking) passes. | python -m threnody_rl.tests.test_parity -> 'all 9 tests passed' (2026-09-17) |
| Built a counterfactual balance tool: stat overrides applied in memory, then baseline and modified 5x5 matchup matrices, per-matchup deltas and a JSON dump, with decisive-game (W/(W+L)) re-analysis. | threnody_rl/tune.py, threnody_rl/analyze_tune.py, threnody_rl/eval.py |

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- The trained agent learned to win on the turn-limit alive-count tiebreak rather than by eliminating opponents, so its win rates are not yet a valid proxy for player-level balance.
- Aggregate win rate is confounded by draws; stat nerfs that turn draws into decisive games can look like buffs.
- Single training seed and single checkpoint; checkpoints are not published.
- The counterfactual tool holds the policy fixed, so the agent does not re-optimise for the changed stats.
- Baseline and modified runs are not common-random-number paired; there are no confidence intervals in tool output.
- Combat-rule and turn-logic parity with the live JavaScript engine has no cross-engine test; only unit data was diffed.
- Predecessor (tabletop prototype) RL code is not in its repository, and its headline metric (win rate against a frozen, first-moving snapshot in one matchup) is not a strength measure.

## Tools

Python, PyTorch, PPO, action-masked actor-critic, frozen-snapshot self-play, NumPy, Flask dashboard
